opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: New Projects and Commissions max £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections max £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications max £5,000; Long-Term Research max £20,000; Research and Travel max £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating in a non-profit capacity for at least 12 months) for New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, and Long-Term Research categories. Individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators for the Research and Travel category. Not open to individuals wishing to develop their own artistic practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding the appreciation of sculpture. Categories: New Projects and Commissions (exhibitions, catalogues, commissions); Acquisitions and Collections (acquisition, conservation, cataloguing, display); Conferences, Lectures and Publications; Long-Term Research grants; and Research and Travel grants for individuals. Applications considered four times per year; the Autumn round is currently open.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000, plus accommodation in Leeds or Hertfordshire for the duration of the fellowship

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators and researchers working on historic and contemporary sculpture (Visiting Research Fellowships); artists developing their practice through research (Artist Research Fellowships); established scholars for longer six-week Senior Fellowships. Only projects related to Henry Moore are considered for fellowships at Studios & Gardens.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute's research facilities in Leeds or Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Applications are currently closed for 2026/27; the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: BA dissertation: £250 cash prize; MA dissertation: £250 cash prize; plus Henry Moore Institute publications to the value of £50, copies of dissertations added to the Research Library, and publication of abstracts

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines whose dissertation was submitted within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertations must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for outstanding extended writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture, awarded to BA and MA students. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
